subject: Can't send message on a closed WebSocket

messages.author: 4be88a5fc86a040f
messages.subject: Can't send message on a closed WebSocket
parts:
Hello.
I am consistently getting this error right after runApp() with window graying out.
Error in .websocket$send(json) : Can't send message on a closed WebSocket
Here are two scenarios for it to happen

1. There's an error inside observe({}), triggered by unexpected user input. Application fails, I debug my code to get rid of the error, save and source the code and re-run application. And it fails immediately with the closed websocket error.  Restarting R session helps, but it is very tedious to do it every time.

2. I place a breakpoint inside a reactive function. Breakpoint is hit, I decide to stop the app and hit "stop" button in the console. When I re-run my app, it fails immediately with the same error. Again, restarting R session helps, but doing this every time makes debugging a pain.

I was unable to reproduce any of these situations on a smaller example, it just doesn't occur. So the issue must be in my app. Has anybody encountered it? I apologize I couldn't be more specific, any general advice is welcome.

R version 3.0.2 (2013-09-25)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)
shiny_0.7.0.99
R studio: 0.98.443

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: Can't send message on a closed WebSocket
parts:
This is something I've encountered before. I believe both (1) and (2)
have to do with leftover reactive expressions and observers. We've
been considering ways to fix the issue, but haven't settled on a good
solution yet.

One workaround which usually works is to run the following a few times
after your app stops. It should clear out old reactive expressions and
observers:
shiny:::flushReact()

-Winston

messages.author: 4be88a5fc86a040f
messages.subject: Re: Can't send message on a closed WebSocket
parts:
Works! Thank you for such a prompt response.
Added to global.R for convenience:

flushReactives <- function(){
    tryCatch(shiny:::flushReact(), error = function(err) flushReactives())
}
flushReactives()
